name: Paneer Manchurian
steps: Pat paneer dry. Mix most cornflour with all-purpose flour, a pinch of salt and enough measured water to make a thin coating; reserve remaining cornflour for the sauce.
Coat paneer cubes lightly and shallow-fry in hot oil until golden at the edges. Drain without overcooking the soft centres.
In a hot wok with a little oil, stir-fry garlic and ginger briefly, then add onion and capsicum; keep the vegetables slightly crisp.
Add soy sauce, ketchup and chilli sauce. Stir remaining cornflour with a splash of water, pour in and bubble until the glossy sauce just coats a spoon.
Toss the fried paneer through the sauce only until coated. Finish with spring onion greens and serve immediately as a dry starter.
tips: Use a sauce with no animal-derived additives; the paneer should stay crisp-edged rather than sitting in gravy.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
